beats.spoken: Super 100s, Super 150s: numbers like these appear on some suit fabrics. They sound like a grade for quality. But they measure just one thing.

data.question: What does it count?
data.source: Woolmark: Introduction to Wovenwear, p. 6 · accessed 02.11.2026

beats.spoken: Go down to a single wool fibre, in cross-section. The Super number describes its mean diameter, measured in microns. A micron is a thousandth of a millimetre. The system comes from the wool body IWTO and is administered by Woolmark.

data.source: Woolmark: Introduction to Wovenwear, p. 6 · accessed 02.11.2026

beats.spoken: Important: the number is an upper limit. Super 100s means a mean of at most 18.75 microns. Super 150s means at most 16.25. Each step of ten lowers the limit by half a micron. The scale runs from Super 80s to Super 250s.

Finer means thinner. Slide the cross-sections on top of each other and you see the difference. It is measured on the finished fabric, with no measuring tolerance, and only for pure new wool with at most five percent decorative yarn. Because the mean diameter can rise during processing, Woolmark advises raw wool that is half a micron to a micron finer.

note.text: on the finished fabric, no tolerance

beats.spoken: Remember: Super 100s is an upper limit for the mean fibre diameter. The number measures nothing else. Follow Suitwerk for menswear with an eye for detail.

data.claim: Menswear with an eye for detail.
